answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear registration bond. Before an agent can wander the marketplace or begin a trading voyage, it must lock a refundable stake that scales with the square of the identities a single funder creates: 1 agent costs 1 unit, but 1,000 sybils cost 1,000,000. An audit agent named Raven ties every bond to its funding origin on-ledger, so the only way to break it is to source 1,000 genuinely independent bankrolls, which erases the economic advantage of cheap mass identities.
